closure_evidence.claim: FALSE POSITIVE — /#menu is a React SPA hash-route (compiled/racine.js RESTORE_ROUTES), not a dead scroll anchor.
closure_evidence.verification_method: Live browser navigation via claude-in-chrome MCP, not just grep or getElementById checks.
closure_evidence.evidence: Navigated to https://www.lecayenne.fr/#menu on the REAL production tab already open in the browser session. document.getElementById('menu') is indeed null (confirming the round-1 grep was technically correct) BUT the page rendered the full functional Menu view: h1/h2/h3 text ['Tout ce qu'on cuisine.', 'Catégories', 'Filtres', ...], 9 categories, 38 products with prices, search box, all fully interactive — screenshot captured and visually confirmed. This proves the CTA genuinely works end-to-end for a real user; round-1's live-repro method (checking getElementById + scrollY only) tested the wrong mechanism (scroll-anchor semantics) against a client-side hash-router. Round-1's underlying P0 claim is therefore a genuine false positive, and the round-2 closure claim holds.

closure_evidence.claim: dessinerBandeau() now has an onerror handler on the vignette , degrading to the same 🎁 emoji fallback used for 'no photo', mirroring chargerPhotos()'s existing pattern.
closure_evidence.verification_method: Read the exact committed roue.html source (lines ~605-661), then reproduced the identical function logic live in a real browser tab against a genuinely broken same-origin image URL, observing the DOM before/after the error event.
closure_evidence.evidence: Source read confirms the onerror handler matches the fix_hint exactly, including the IIFE capture of `vignette` to avoid the classic var-in-for-loop closure bug (same pattern already used by chargerPhotos()'s IIFE for its own im.onerror). Live repro: created a vignette+img with the exact onerror callback from the source, pointed the img at a same-origin URL that returns 404 (curl-verified: '404 time=0.002760'), and after the error event fired, the vignette's innerHTML became exactly '🎁', aria-hidden='true', textContent='🎁' — identical to the 'no photo' fallback path, zero broken-image icon. (Note: an intermediate attempt using `img.loading='lazy'` inside the automation tab did not fire the error event within 3s — traced to the automation tab's lazy-load heuries not the fix logic itself; removing `loading=lazy` isolated and confirmed the onerror handler works correctly. This is a methodology artifact of the browser-automation environment, not a defect — the project's own committed Playwright spec exercises the real DOM in a real Playwright-driven browser and independently proves the same behavior, see roue-fond-carrousel-redirection-2026-08-13.spec.js results below.) Independently, running the project's own regression spec (not written by me) also asserts 'photo cassée : le cassé est RETIRÉ du DOM (pas d'icône image cassée du navigateur)' — PASS, and 'la vignette bascule sur le MÊME fallback emoji que pas de photo du tout' — PASS.

closure_evidence.claim: New tests/e2e/roue-account-cross-cutting-2026-08-13.spec.js covers a real config-fetch and a keyboard pass on /admin/roue-borne, using page.context().request.get() instead of page.evaluate(fetch) to avoid Debugbar's fetch-interception leaking the x-api-key header into the committed .dom.html.
closure_evidence.verification_method: Ran the spec live (`npx playwright test ... --project=chromium --workers=1 --retries=0`); read the spec source to confirm the causal mechanism claimed; extracted the REAL literal API key value from .env (resolveApiKey() -> MIX_API_KEY) and grepped it, plus the generic string 'x-api-key', against every committed artifact byte-for-byte via `git show HEAD:<path>`.
closure_evidence.evidence: 2 passed, 5.8s: 'clavier seul sur /admin/roue-borne : aucun piège de focus dans le contenu réel' and 'GET /api/frontend/wheel/config répond 200, capture complète émise'. Spec source (lines 135-146) documents the exact causal claim: Debugbar intercepts page-context fetch() and replays request headers (incl. x-api-key) into its own panel, which lands in wheel-config-200.dom.html; page.context().request.get() makes the real network call OUTSIDE the page's JS execution context, invisible to Debugbar's AJAX interceptor. Verified empirically: grepped the literal .env value of MIX_API_KEY (b6d68vy2-m7g5-20r0-5275-h103w73453q120) against all 8 committed files in tests/captures/roue-account-cross-cutting-2026-08-13/ at HEAD — zero matches. Also grepped the generic string 'x-api-key' case-insensitively against the same 8 files — zero matches anywhere. The claimed security fix is real and effective, not just asserted.

closure_evidence.claim: Dead .etapes/.etapes li/.etapes em CSS removed from roue.html; tests-e2e/roue-2026-08-09.regression.js updated to assert the real progressive-reveal invariant (ecran0 visible, ecran1/2/3 hidden) instead of the removed etapes===3 count, now 10/10.
closure_evidence.verification_method: grep for '.etapes' in the committed roue.html (only a comment referencing the removal remains, no CSS rule); read the new assertion in full to reason about vacuousness; ran the regression spec live.
closure_evidence.evidence: grep '.etapes' roue.html returns exactly 1 hit — a code comment documenting the 2026-08-13 removal, no CSS rule. The new assertion (revelationProgressiveOk) checks four concrete DOM element states via getElementById + .hidden: e0 present and NOT hidden, e1/e2/e3 present AND hidden. This is not vacuous — if progressive reveal were broken (e.g. all screens shown at once, or ecran0 itself hidden), at least one of the four boolean terms would flip and the check would fail. Live run: `node tests-e2e/roue-2026-08-09.regression.js` against http://127.0.0.1:8899 → 10/10, including the new line 'révélation progressive au chargement : seule l'étape 0 est visible, 1/2/3 restent masquées — true'.
